sections.label: Committee report and CareShield Life name
sections.summary: The Committee submitted its report in May 2018, and the Report was accepted, including the recommendation on the new name CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Committee submitted its report in May 2018, and we have accepted the Report, including the recommendation on the new name “CareShield Life”.

sections.label: Singaporeans aged 65 and above
sections.summary: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above, compared to one in seven today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above, compared to one in seven today.

sections.label: Long-term care government expenditure increase
sections.summary: Government expenditure in long-term care increased six-fold from $140 million in 2011 to around $800 million in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our Government expenditure in long-term care increased six-fold from $140 million in 2011 to around $800 million in 2016.

sections.label: Projected severe disability at 65
sections.summary: Projections are that one in two Singaporeans healthy at age 65 could become severely disabled at some point and require long-term care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In fact, our projections are that one in two Singaporeans who are healthy at age 65 could become severely disabled at some point in their lifetime and require long-term care.

sections.label: Median duration of disability
sections.summary: The median duration of disability is four years, but three in 10 could remain severely disabled for 10 years or more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The median duration of disability is four years, but three in 10 could remain severely disabled for 10 years or more.

sections.label: CareShield Life funding and coverage
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced $2 billion to support CareShield Life, and from 2020 all Singapore residents born in 1980 or later will be covered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Earlier in the Budget this year, the Minister for Finance announced that we would put aside $2 billion to support CareShield Life, and this is on top of the Government’s spending in our intermediate and long-term care facilities and services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: From 2020, all Singapore residents born in 1980 or later will be covered by CareShield Life.

sections.label: CareShield Life incentives and MediSave premiums
sections.summary: Existing cohorts joining CareShield Life in 2021 get participation incentives, cannot lose coverage, can get Additional Premium Support, and pay premiums via MediSave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Second, we will provide participation incentives of between $500 and $2,500 to all Singapore Citizens from existing cohorts who join CareShield Life in the first two years from 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Third, once they have joined the scheme, they will not lose coverage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Should they find themselves unable to pay for premiums later on even after subsidies and incentives, we will provide Additional Premium Support similar to future cohorts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To help Singaporeans afford Careshield Life, premiums can be fully paid for by MediSave, including the MediSave of immediate family members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will also ensure that Singaporeans currently insured on ElderShield can seamlessly upgrade to CareShield Life, and that the premiums they have already paid are taken into account when we compute the premiums they need to pay for CareShield Life.

sections.label: Example premium and payout
sections.summary: A person receives a $500 incentive over 10 years, giving an estimated net starting annual premium of $216, and around $1,000 monthly for life if severely disabled at 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In addition, he will also receive a participation incentive of $500 that will be spread over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, his estimated net starting annual premium in 2021 would be $216, which amounts to $18 per month, and he can pay this using MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If he becomes severely disabled at age 67, he will receive around $1,000 per month for life.

sections.label: Bill for CareShield Life fund
sections.summary: A Bill will be introduced next year to set up the CareShield Life fund and independent Council and effect the scheme by 2020 for future cohorts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will share more on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We intend to introduce a Bill next year to set up the CareShield Life fund and the independent Council and to effect the scheme by 2020 for future cohorts.

sections.label: MediSave cash withdrawals for disabled
sections.summary: From 2020, severely disabled Singapore residents aged 30 and above can withdraw cash from their own or their spouse's MediSave accounts for long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: From 2020, severely disabled Singapore residents aged 30 and above will be able to withdraw cash from their own or their spouse’s MediSave accounts to support their long-term care needs.

sections.label: Enhancements to long-term care financing
sections.summary: The Government is enhancing risk-pooling through CareShield Life and allowing MediSave cash withdrawals, and will intensify public education and communications efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, we are enhancing risk-pooling through a new long-term care insurance scheme, CareShield Life, and the Government will do its part by providing significant support for Singaporeans joining the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Second, we are allowing more flexibility in the use of MediSave by allowing severely disabled Singaporeans to make cash withdrawals for long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: These enhancements to our long-term care financing system are new, and we expect that Singaporeans will need time to digest and understand them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will intensify our public education and communications efforts, and work with community partners and other stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We hope to give Singaporeans greater assurance and peace of mind on their long-term care needs.

sections.label: ElderShield enhancement to CareShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker says enhancing ElderShield to CareShield Life is timely and significant as an important piece of the social safety net.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But all of these could lead us to greater dependence on other people for our everyday activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, I feel that the enhancement of ElderShield to CareShield Life is timely and significant, as it constitutes an important piece of our social safety net, which until now, I would submit, has been deficient, in terms of the adequacy of our national long-term disability insurance system.

sections.label: Payouts and premium adjustments
sections.summary: The GPC agrees payouts should track general and medical inflation, and CareShield Life premiums will also need adjusting for financial sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One, the GPC concurs that payouts be adjusted to keep pace with general and medical inflation and, in order for this to be financially sustainable, CareShield Life premiums will also need to be adjusted.

sections.label: Removing gender-differentiated premiums
sections.summary: The report recognised the actuarial basis for women's higher premiums but repeated the call to remove gender differentiation, as in MediShield.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Two, in our report, we recognised the actuarial basis for the higher premiums that women pay but would like to repeat our call that this gender differentiation be removed, in line, for example, with other insurance programmes, such as medical and hospitalisation insurance, such as MediShield.

sections.label: Underestimated risk of severe disability
sections.summary: The risk of becoming significantly disabled may be as high as one in two, but is often underestimated, especially by the young.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The prospect of becoming significantly disabled in our lifetime is very real and, by some estimates, may be as high as one in two, but this risk is often underestimated or discounted, and quite understandably, particularly by the young.

sections.label: ElderShield severe disability definition
sections.summary: ElderShield covered severely disabled persons, defined as unable to do at least three of six activities of daily living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ElderShield was designed to cover “severely disabled” persons, defined as persons unable to do at least three of the six activities of daily living (ADLs), that is, washing, dressing, feeding, toileting, walking and transferring.

sections.label: Mandatory contributions for younger Singaporeans
sections.summary: As a compulsory scheme, CareShield requires all Singaporeans born in 1980 or later to contribute mandatorily for 37 years, from age 30 to 67.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since CareShield is going to be a compulsory disability scheme, all Singaporeans born in 1980 or later will be making mandatory contributions for 37 years, from age 30 to 67.

sections.label: Women paying higher premiums
sections.summary: It has been proposed that CareShield Life premiums be differentiated by gender, with women paying more due to longer life expectancy and higher severe disability risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, why is CareShield making women pay more?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It has been proposed that premiums for CareShield Life be differentiated by gender.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Women will be asked to pay higher premiums, because, as the Committee says at Chapter 8, women have a longer life expectancy and have higher risk of severe disability.

sections.label: Gender-differentiated versus unisex premiums
sections.summary: Setting premiums as gender-differentiated or unisex is a stand on society's values.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After all, deciding whether to set premiums as gender-differentiated or on a unisex basis is taking a stand on our society’s values.

sections.label: Prof Barr on unisex long-term care
sections.summary: Prof Barr argues long-term care social insurance should not account for women living longer, giving three reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the issue of women living longer, however, Prof Barr argues that social insurance schemes for long-term care should not take this into account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He offers several reasons for this: “First, if the insurance is mandatory, there is little or no distortionary effect from charging men and women a premium based on joint probabilities; second, there are obvious political difficulties from imposing on women a significantly higher contribution rate than men; and finally, the use of unisex tables can be defended as a simple value judgement”.

sections.label: Signal of higher women's premiums
sections.summary: The passage asks what signal is sent by requiring women to pay higher premiums while doing more unpaid caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What signal do we send to our mothers, wives, sisters and daughters by requiring them to pay higher premiums, while expecting them to do more caregiving for free?

sections.label: Support for CareShield Life with issues
sections.summary: The speaker supports CareShield Life's principle but raises the three ADLs test and unisex premiums as critical issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have stated my general support for the principle underlying universal and compulsory long-term care insurance that the CareShield Life scheme represents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have, however, raised two issues which I believe are critical to the Scheme’s success, namely, whether the qualifying “three ADLs test” is too rigid and onerous, and asking for the premiums to be set on a unisex basis if the scheme is truly to be universal and inclusive.

sections.label: Committee report and Government acceptance
sections.summary: The committee report was dated 25 May 2018, the day the Minister signified acceptance, announced in the press two days later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The report of the committee was dated 25 May 2018, on the same day the Minister signified the Government's acceptance and, in two days, the acceptance was announced in the press.

sections.label: ElderShield premiums and actuarial verification
sections.summary: The passage asks whether ElderShield premiums rose with payouts and whether independent actuarial verification justified premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, for example, when ElderShield payouts were increased, were ElderShield premiums also increased?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And when we compare the premiums of $3.3 billion collected with the payout of $133 million in claims, whether the Government conducted an independent actuarial verification to justify the premiums that continued to be collected for ElderShield, and whether those considerations guided the Government in the calculation of the premiums for CareShield.

sections.label: Transparency of CareShield Life computations
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Government will consider statutory mechanisms, principles and releasing actuarial data for transparency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I am wondering if, for transparency, the Government will consider the following, such as statutory mechanisms to adjust premiums in future, statutory principles to be applied in the adjustments of payouts, what happens when we need to freeze or lower payouts in the event of a squeeze on the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And at the very least, as suggested by Dr Jeremy Lim in his article “Why Singapore needs the new CareShield Life” published by Today Online on 5 June 2018, could we have raw data and assumptions in actuarial computations being made available to the industry and academics so that the transparency of the computations can be clear to all?

sections.label: Oversight of insurance scheme
sections.summary: The speaker asks who oversees the schemes and how the Government gained expertise, noting 40% opted out of ElderShield.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second question: who ultimately has oversight of the overlays, or potential gaps, among the schemes and the toll that they may take on Singaporeans’ CPF monies?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how the Government has acquired the necessary expertise and resources to manage the insurance scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The current ElderShield Scheme has seen around 40% eligible of Singaporeans opting out because of the perception of low payouts, amongst other reasons.

sections.label: One in two disability statistic
sections.summary: The speaker raises concern about the statistic that one in two Singaporeans become severely disabled in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One major concern I have, which the Minister briefly expanded upon, is the statistics that the ElderShield Review Committee and many mainstream media outlets zeroed-in on of one in two Singaporeans becoming severely disabled in their lifetime.

sections.label: ElderShield rebates to CPF members
sections.summary: The Ministry confirmed two ElderShield rebates were given to CPF members, in 2007 and 2012, totalling $130 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From a Parliamentary Question filed by my colleague Assoc Prof Daniel Goh in 2017, the Ministry confirmed that two ElderShield rebates have been given to CPF members enrolled in the scheme – one in 2007 and another in 2012 – to the tune of $130 million in total.

sections.label: Freedom of Information for CareShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a Freedom of Information framework and an information officer for CareShield Life requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, I would call for the Government to consider implementing a Freedom of Information framework in the administration of CareShield Life and appoint an information officer to the Independent Council who would respond to public requests for information about any aspect of CareShield Life for a reasonable administrative fee.

sections.label: Reviewing gender neutral CareShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker supports calls to review whether CareShield Life can be made gender neutral, citing inclusivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, my Workers’ Party colleagues and, I note, the Chairman of the Healthcare GPC have spoken about reviewing whether CareShield Life can be made gender neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I strongly support this call in the name of inclusivity and in parallel with the scheme’s philosophy of each cohort looking after itself.

sections.label: MediSave top-up tax relief
sections.summary: Calls on the Government to consider extending tax relief to CPF members who top up loved ones' MediSave accounts until the Basic Healthcare Sum is met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this vein, I would also call on the Government to consider extending tax relief to CPF members who top up the CPF MediSave accounts of their loved ones, regardless of gender, until the Basic Healthcare Sum is met, similar to the tax relief cap on top-ups to the Special Account currently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such a move would enhance the ability of CPF members’ MediSave accounts to support future increases in CareShield Life and other compulsory premiums, generate greater interest for members and give them some peace of mind for their loved ones at the same time.

sections.label: ElderShield Committee recommendations
sections.summary: The ElderShield Committee's recommendations address three objectives the speaker concurs with: greater inclusivity, better protection and affordability.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recommendations put forward by the ElderShield Committee to strengthen our social safety net for Singaporeans address three key objectives which I fully concur: greater inclusivity, better protection and affordability.

sections.label: Government-run CareShield Life scheme
sections.summary: The scheme should be headed by the Government rather than outsourced to third party insurance companies to prevent profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The scheme should not be outsourced to third party insurance companies but instead be headed by the Government to prevent third party insurance companies from exploiting CareShield Life for the main reason of profiteering.

sections.label: Compulsory CareShield Life from age 30
sections.summary: CareShield Life being compulsory for all citizens from 30 years old means a considerable sum of insurance monies for CPF Board to manage.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With CareShield Life being compulsory for all citizens from 30 years old, it will be a considerable sum of insurance monies to be managed by CPF Board.

sections.label: Gender premiums and pre-existing disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker notes gender-differentiated premiums and the gender wage gap, supports reviewing schemes for severely disabled existing cohorts, and asks how Government will protect those with pre-existing disabilities excluded from CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the gender-differentiated CareShield Life premiums reflect the differences in risks between men and women, we should also acknowledge and consider the economic disparity stemming from the gender wage gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, the gender wage gap of 19% to 40% in some industries do persist for various reasons and this makes women more financially vulnerable if they do not have enough for their retirement and also their healthcare needs and payment of premium.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the committee's call for the Government to review the existing schemes and subsidies to assist Singaporeans who are already severely disabled in the existing cohorts since they will be excluded from CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, why have such differentiated approaches for existing cohorts of Singaporeans with pre-existing disabilities under CareShield Life, whereas universal coverage was introduced with MediShield Life covering those with pre-existing conditions?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will the Government be offering additional protection to cover people with pre-existing disabilities but are excluded from CareShield Life?

sections.label: Adequacy of $600 payout
sections.summary: The speaker repeats the concern that a $600 payout in the year 2020 will still be inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Today, I still want to raise the same concern that a $600 payout in the year 2020 will still be inadequate.

sections.label: Premium and payout amounts
sections.summary: The annual premium is around $206 million with opt-outs, while the payout amount is about $8.32 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The annual premium is around $206 million with opt-outs, while the payout amount is about $8.32 million.

sections.label: CareShield Life claims and premiums
sections.summary: It asks how onerous claiming CareShield Life is and how soon patients can claim, citing ElderShield figures and a 2020 Government takeover.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will it be onerous for such patients to claim for CareShield Life and how soon after being afflicted can such patients claim?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It had been reported that private insurers collected some $2.6 billion in premiums for ElderShield and only about $133 million had been paid out in claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2020, the Government will take over the coverage, thus there is no risk for the private insurers for future claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is a difference in premium payments between men and women with CareShield Life.

sections.label: Assistance for severely disabled
sections.summary: It asks what assistance is available for those not covered under CareShield Life who face severe disability and financial difficulty, and calls for homecare and community care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What kind of assistance is available to assist those, not covered under CareShield Life, being struck with severe disability and have financial difficulty?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I feel that MOH needs to develop homecare and community care, presently very scarce, as quickly as possible to cater for our fast escalating need to help severely disabled people remain in their own homes.

sections.label: Incentives for preventive health
sections.summary: It asks MOH to help Singaporeans stay healthy and prevent and control chronic diseases, and to consider premium discounts tied to CareShield Life and MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, as a strong advocate of preventive medicine myself, may I beseech MOH to endeavor fullest to assist Singaporeans to keep healthy and to prevent chronic diseases and to have good control of their chronic diseases, should they have them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, will MOH consider incentives, for example, premium discount, tied to our insurance schemes, CareShield Life and MediShield Life, to nudge or motivate people to achieve better health and to keep chronic diseases at bay?

sections.label: CareShield enhancements and eligibility
sections.summary: The enhancements include lifelong payments, a $600 monthly payment in two years, and eligibility for those unable to perform any three of six daily activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The enhancements include lifelong payments, compared to the six-year maximum at present under ElderShield.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When it comes into force in two years’ time, the monthly payment will be $600, that is, $200 higher than the present $400 under ElderShield.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among six daily activities, if you cannot perform any three, then you will be considered "severely disabled" and eligible for claims under CareShield.

sections.label: Committee premium support recommendations
sections.summary: The Committee recommends permanent means-tested premium subsidies, transitional subsidies, and additional premium support so no one loses coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Committee recommends Government support through: (a) permanent means-tested premium subsidies; (b) transitional subsidies; and (c) additional premium support for Singaporeans who are unable to pay their premiums, even after subsidies, so that no one will lose coverage.

sections.label: CareShield Life and US healthcare
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes CareShield Life as a step toward accessible, affordable long-term healthcare planning, noting America has not struck a good balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In America, they have yet to be able to strike a good balance in ensuring that the health of the population is taken care of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I welcome the CareShield Life initiative as a step in the right direction to provide Singaporeans with an accessible, affordable means to plan for their long-term healthcare needs.

sections.label: Premium subsidy percentage increase
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider increasing the premium subsidy percentage, currently estimated at about 20% to 30%, to ensure affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Would the Government also consider increasing the percentage of premium subsidy provided, currently estimated at about 20% to 30%, to ensure affordability?

sections.label: Converting all ElderShield policyholders
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider converting all ElderShield policyholders to CareShield and absorbing the additional premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While there are options to allow for existing ElderShield policyholders to convert to CareShield, could the Government consider converting all ElderShield policyholders and absorbing the additional premiums to do so?

sections.label: ElderShield conversion affordability and health
sections.summary: The speaker says many ElderShield joiners may feel they missed out and cannot afford conversion, and suggests premium rates depend on the applicant's health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Many of those who had joined ElderShield will feel that they missed out on the benefits of CareShield Life and may not be able to afford the conversion to the new higher premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I would also like to suggest that the premium rates to be paid should depend on the health of the applicant.

sections.label: Auto-enrolment age and disability criteria
sections.summary: Under the proposed plan, only policyholders aged 41-50 in 2020 who are not severely disabled will be auto-enrolled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under the proposed plan, only policyholders aged 41-50 in 2020 and who are not severely disabled will be auto-enrolled.

sections.label: Opt-out scheme and coverage questions
sections.summary: The speaker requests CareShield Life be opt-out for former ElderShield opt-outs and asks about severe disabilities before age 30 and coverage from age 21.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As CareShield Life will be administered by the Government, compared to coverage from private insurers, it will provide greater assurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I request that CareShield Life be made an opt-out scheme so that all who have previously opted out of ElderShield will be covered this time under the new scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, may I ask the Minister, on average, based on past data, how many Singaporeans have suffered severe disabilities before the age of 30?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can we also explore the idea of starting disability coverage from the age 21 and extending coverage grants to National Servicemen to show our appreciation for their services to our country?

sections.label: Women pay higher premiums
sections.summary: The first concern with inclusivity is that women pay premiums 25% higher than men.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first concern with inclusivity is that women pay significantly higher premiums compared to men, 25% higher.

sections.label: Auto-enrolment of ElderShield members
sections.summary: The second concern is the auto-enrolment of ElderShield members aged 41-50 in 2021 into CareShield Life with an opt-out option.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second concern I have with inclusivity the auto-enrolment of ElderShield members aged 41-50 in 2021 into CareShield Life with the option of opting out.

sections.label: Division in auto-enrolment
sections.summary: The concern is that dividing auto-enrolment between those in their 40s and those in their 50s and 60s would create a lost generation of retiring workers with less long-term disability protection.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My concern is that this division in auto-enrolment between those in their 40s and those in their 50s and 60s would create a lost generation of retiring workers with less protection for long-term disability when they are the ones who would need it most in the coming decade of the ageing society.

sections.label: CareShield Life affordability compromise
sections.summary: The last issue is whether CareShield Life compromises on affordability, noting the ESRC Report that one in two healthy people aged 65 and above could become severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The last issue is that in trying to be inclusive and sustainable, is CareShield Life compromising on affordability?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I was shocked to read in the opening of the ESRC Report that one in two healthy people aged 65 and above today could become severely disabled in their lifetime.

sections.label: Government support for needy groups
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government would support and subsidise needy groups so CareShield Life does not exclude or disenfranchise any Singaporean, and asks why women pay higher premiums.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, after all, the tradeoffs have been made, I hope the Government would step in to support and subsidise needy groups when necessary to make sure the CareShield Life balancing act does not exclude or disenfranchise any Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is especially since social risk-pooling would mean the Government would save on providing direct social support to the needy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It would be most uplifting for our vulnerable fellow citizens to know that they are being supported and carried up by their fellow Singaporeans with the help of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are but a few points which I would like to raise, one of which is: why is it that women have to pay a higher premium for CareShield Life?

sections.label: Figure per 1,000 births
sections.summary: The figure was 4.8 per 1,000 births in 2016, down from 7.1 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The figure was 4.8 per 1,000 births in 2016, down from 7.1 in 2015.

sections.label: Actuarial considerations for pre-existing conditions
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to explain the actuarial considerations for excluding persons with pre-existing conditions from ElderShield to CareShield Life conversion.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, could the Minister explain what are the actuarial considerations for the exclusion of any person with pre-existing conditions for conversion from ElderShield to CareShield Life?

sections.label: Elderly disability percentage statistics
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister what percentage of the elderly is likely to suffer disability, based on statistical studies.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From statistical studies, can the Minister share with the House what percentage of the elderly is likely to suffer from disability of one form or another?

sections.label: Lifetime payouts for severely disabled
sections.summary: The proposed lifetime payouts last as long as the claimant remains severely disabled, giving greater assurance to claimants and families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The proposed lifetime payouts, for as long as the claimant remains severely disabled, will provide greater assurance for claimants and their families.

sections.label: Compulsory CareShield Life plan
sections.summary: The enhanced plan, CareShield Life, is recommended to be compulsory for all adults with contributions from age 30, offering better benefits and a more inclusive definition of severe disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The proposed enhanced plan, also known as CareShield Life, is recommended to be compulsory for all adults and for contribution to start as young as from age 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: It will have the legislative backing and muscle to achieve risk-pooling coverage at an unprecedented scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Thus, it is able to offer not just better benefits, but a more inclusive definition of severe disability as well.

sections.label: Government target for long-term care cost
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister what percentage the Government targets the scheme to contribute to projected long-term care costs in 2020, and how much subsidies would fall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: With the proposed transformation of ElderShield to CareShield Life, could the Minister reveal how much, in percentage, the Government is targeting for the proposed scheme to contribute to the projected cost of long-term care in Singapore when it is made compulsory for all in 2020, and how much would the Government subsidies come down correspondingly as a result?

sections.label: Release of actuarial computation report
sections.summary: A Member urges the Government to release the actuarial computation report and the thinking behind CareShield Life premiums, since the scheme is not for profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The only thing left is for the Government to be transparent with the actuarial calculations for premiums since the proposed scheme is meant to be not for profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: On this note, I urge the Government to release the actuarial computation report and the thinking that went behind the formulation of the premiums for CareShield Life.

sections.label: CareShield Life payouts features
sections.summary: Passage notes lifetime payouts instead of five or six years under ElderShield 300 and 400, and increased payouts over time starting from $600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In particular, two main features are noteworthy, as stated by hon Members: the payouts for life as opposed to the current five or six years under ElderShield 300 and ElderShield 400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The second feature is, of course, the increased payouts over time, starting from $600.

sections.label: CareShield Life coverage and ADLs
sections.summary: MOH stated no one would lose CareShield Life coverage due to financial difficulties; some Members sought dropping three ADLs to two, but the committee report says one in two Singaporeans may become disabled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The point was probably put across more colourfully as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I find it comforting though that MOH has categorically stated that no one would lose their CareShield Life coverage due to financial difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Some hon Members have asked for requirement of three ADLs to be dropped to two ADLs, justifying it on the basis of the current low claim history and the opportunity arising from risk-pooling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, I read in the committee report that one in two Singaporeans may become disabled some time in their lives.

sections.label: ElderShield report disability sentence
sections.summary: Passage quotes an ElderShield report sentence that one in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 could become severely disabled in their lifetime, and asks whether premiums were set on that assumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One sentence in the Eldershield report read: "One in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 could become severely disabled in their lifetime and may need long-term care." Were premiums set based on the assumption that one in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 will become severely disabled in future?

sections.label: Premium rebates and adjustment council
sections.summary: Passage cites the ElderShield report's call for an independent council to advise on premium and payout adjustments, and page 88 on insurers returning 50% of surplus, then asks if CareShield Life rebates are discretionary or mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the executive summary of the ElderShield report, it is stated: “An independent council should be set up to advise the Government on premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.” According to page 88 of the ESRC Report, in the context of the existing ElderShield scheme, the premium rebate is a feature that provides for the three insurers that administer ElderShield to return 50% of any accumulated surplus to existing ElderShield policyholders, if the actual claims experience turns out to be better than what was projected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For CareShield Life, will premium rebates be discretionary or mandatory?

sections.label: Government administration of scheme
sections.summary: Passage states the report recommends the Government administer the scheme, unlike ElderShield which is operated by Aviva, Great Eastern and NTUC Income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, on efficiency, the report recommends that the Government administer the scheme, unlike ElderShield which is operated by Aviva, Great Eastern and NTUC Income.

sections.label: CareShield funds and GIC bonds
sections.summary: Passage asks whether investing reserves through bonds issued to GIC would be pursued for CareShield funds, as is partly done for CPF monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the practice of investing reserves through the issuance of bonds to the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC) be pursued for CareShield funds, as is currently undertaken, in part, for CPF monies?

sections.label: Day care and home care alternatives
sections.summary: Day care, home care and integrated home and day care have the most room for further development, with AIC starting IHDC pilots in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of these, perhaps the one set of alternatives within the ecosystem that has the most room for further consideration and development is day care, home care, as well as integrated home and day care (IHDC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I know that various IHDC trial schemes and initiatives are underway and that the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) started IHDC pilots in 2016.

sections.label: Hong Kong day care centres
sections.summary: The Hong Kong Social Welfare Department lists around 80 day care centres and units on its website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Hong Kong Social Welfare Department lists around 80 day care centres and units on its website.

sections.label: Take-up of sector employment
sections.summary: It asks what results there have been in nudging Singaporeans to take up employment in this sector and volunteer with VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What have been the results thus far in terms of nudging Singaporeans to take up full-time or part-time employment in this sector, as well as to volunteer with the voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) which provide many of such services?

sections.label: CareShield Life income for care needs
sections.summary: CareShield Life ensures that with a largely affordable annual premium, policyholders have an income for daily and care needs when unable to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: CareShield Life will ensure that with a largely affordable annual premium per year, policyholders will have an income for their daily and care needs even when they are unable to work.

sections.label: Premiums paid until age 67
sections.summary: Premiums are paid only until age 67, after which the insured continues to receive lifelong coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: All it takes is one freak accident or serious illness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It would be crucial to note that premiums only have to be paid for until one has reached the age of 67, after which, the insured will continue to receive lifelong coverage.

sections.label: Premium support and enrolment rules
sections.summary: Policyholders who cannot afford premiums can apply for Additional Premium Support; CareShield Life is mandatory for those aged 30 to 40 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For policyholders who cannot afford to pay premiums even after premium subsidies, I am glad to note that they can apply for assistance from the Additional Premium Support scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While CareShield Life will be mandatory for those who will be aged between 30 and 40 in 2020, encouraging those who do not fall into this group to sign up for it will be a big challenge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I note that younger ElderShield 400 policyholders aged 41 to 50 in 2020 will be auto-enrolled into CareShield Life, and they may opt out and have their premiums returned within two years of auto-enrolment should they wish to.

sections.label: CareShield Life complexity concerns
sections.summary: The Government shared detailed plans on CareShield Life incentives, procedures and premiums, but the general consensus is that it is all too complex.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government has shared detailed plans on incentives, procedures and premiums for taking up or switching to CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, the general consensus is that, on top of MediSave, MediShield Life and Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), it is all too complex even for the average literate Singaporean.

sections.label: Overlapping private insurance coverage
sections.summary: Some people with private disability insurance worry about paying for overlapping coverage, and the speaker suggests integrating a CareShield component into insurance policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One crucial factor to consider is that some people would have purchased private insurance policies for disabilities, and they would be concerned about whether they would be paying unnecessarily for overlapping coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Especially for those on a tight budget and can only afford one policy, would it be wise to give up their existing policy in light of CareShield?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If the Government could work with private insurers, as with the case of IPs, integrating a CareShield component into relevant insurance policies and allowing MediSave payments for that component, I think it will be a welcome move.

sections.label: Severe disabilities definition
sections.summary: CareShield Life provides payouts for those with severe disabilities, defined as being unable to perform three of the six ADLs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The proposed CareShield Life provides payouts for those deemed to be suffering from "severe disabilities" and this is defined as a person being unable to perform three of the six ADLs.

sections.label: Payout quantum of $600
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Committee decided on the payout quantum of $600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Third, I would also like to also ask how did the Committee decide on the payout quantum of $600.

sections.label: Transitional subsidies for CareShield Life
sections.summary: The Committee proposed transitional subsidies of up to $250 spread over the first five years to help Singaporeans ease into CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As part of the initial rollout of CareShield Life, the Committee has proposed to provide transitional subsidies of up to $250, spread over the first five years, to help Singaporeans ease into the new scheme.

sections.label: Permanent subsidy and women's premiums
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the transitional subsidy could be made permanent, and notes premiums for women are projected to be around 25% higher than men's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider making this transitional subsidy permanent, beyond the first five years, for future cohorts of Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is projected that premiums for women will be around 25% higher than those for men of the same cohort.

sections.label: Long-term care demand rise
sections.summary: Demand for long-term care in severe disability is projected to rise from 29,000 cases in 2014 to 69,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The demand for long-term care in the event of a severe disability will go up, from 29,000 cases in 2014 to a projected figure of 69,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Subsidies for long-term care
sections.summary: Transitional subsidies for five years and permanent means-tested subsidies of up to 30% will help lower- to middle-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is so, even for the lower income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There will be transitional subsidies for the first five years so that people have a good runway to plan and reorder their budget if they need to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There will also be permanent means-tested subsidies of up to 30% to help lower- to middle-income Singaporeans.

sections.label: Annual premium for males
sections.summary: The annual premium is about $227 for males in the sixth year of the scheme, aged 30 at launch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In contrast, what we are looking at is about $227 annual premium for males, for the sixth year in the scheme, for those who are 30 years old when the scheme was launched.

sections.label: Swiss long-term care premiums
sections.summary: Swiss long-term care premiums are 2.55% of income, with childless people paying 0.25% more, and average annual premium was $5,386 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As of last year, long-term care insurance premiums are 2.55% of the income, split equally between employer and employee, with those without children paying an extra 0.25% of their income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Although the pay-as-you-go scheme in Switzerland faces less concerns about being sustainable, a concern is that the premiums are expensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There, the health insurance covers up to 60 hours of care services a week, but with premiums from birth to life and varying by insurer, age, gender and insurance plan, the average annual premium in 2015 was $5,386.

sections.label: Singapore medical inflation ranking
sections.summary: Singapore still ranks high in medical inflation, though it decreased from 20% in 2014 to 9.6% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In April this year, although there was an overall decrease from 20% in 2014 to 9.6% last year, Singapore still ranks high in terms of medical inflation.

sections.label: Inflation reduces money value
sections.summary: Assuming 2% annual general inflation, $600 now would be worth about $430 in 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Assuming that general inflation is 2% per year, $600 now would be worth about $430 10 years later in what it can buy.

sections.label: Universal coverage from age 30
sections.summary: CareShield Life recommends universal coverage regardless of financial status or pre-existing disability, with cohorts aged 30 to 40 enrolled at launch and later cohorts at age 30.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The recommendation for universal coverage, regardless of financial status or pre-existing disability for future cohorts of Singaporeans starting from age 30, is one that is key for this CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In 2020, cohorts aged 30 to 40 will be enrolled upon the launch of this enhanced scheme, with subsequent cohorts enrolled when they turn 30.

sections.label: Compulsory participation and women's premiums
sections.summary: The compulsory and inclusive nature of participation raises the question of why women need to pay higher premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: On this point of being inclusive and the fact that participation is compulsory, it does beg the question on why women need to pay higher premiums.

sections.label: Higher payout and lifetime coverage
sections.summary: CareShield Life offers a higher payout than ElderShield and provides lifetime coverage as ongoing support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: One key point about CareShield Life is that it offers a higher payout than the current ElderShield Plan and, more importantly, it recognises the fact that it is an ongoing support and, therefore, lifetime coverage.

sections.label: Premium principles and affordability subsidies
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to share the principles used to determine premiums, and notes subsidies to keep premiums affordable for lower and middle-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the actual principles that were used to determine premiums?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: There are also commitments made to support lower and middle-income Singaporeans to keep premium affordable with the permanent means-tested premium subsidies, the transitional subsidies, as well as the Enhanced Premium Support for Singaporeans still unable to afford their premiums even after the subsidies.

sections.label: Annual value as means-test criterion
sections.summary: The passage asks about using residence annual value for means assessment, noting that AV above $21,000 disqualifies individuals even if they are lower income and do not own the property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For means-testing, apart from the fact that the usage of the scheme and the payouts will be dependent on the strict criteria for the three ADLs, the means-testing for the subsidies and the eligibility criteria are a point that I would like to touch on and would like to ask with regard to the use of the annual value (AV) of a residence as a criterion for means assessment because, if the annual value is above $21,000, what it would mean is that, automatically, it will disqualify the individual from eligibility even if he or she is of lower income because he may be living in a residence out of the goodwill of family members and may not own that property.

sections.label: Residents in private homes above AV
sections.summary: Half of the residents in the speaker's ward live in private condominiums and landed homes with AVs above $21,000, and not all own these properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The reason why I am highlighting this is that half of the residents in my ward live in private condominiums and landed homes and their AVs are above the $21,000 criterion and not all of them own these properties and many do live with their family members and some are seniors and have retired as well.

sections.label: Advisory support for CareShield Life
sections.summary: MP asks MOH to consider advisory support to guide ES300 and ES400 members assessing whether to join CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, the communication of the scheme, and especially for those who are on ES300 and ES400, the encouragement for them, if they are eligible to go on to CareShield Life, is not as straightforward in terms of understanding, given the incentives that are provided as well as the various complexities around the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, I hope that, besides the tools and the information provided, MOH would consider setting up an advisory support to provide guidance for this segment as they do the assessment of whether to join CareShield Life or not.

sections.label: CareShield Life coverage and premiums
sections.summary: CareShield Life offers lifetime cash payouts for severe disability, better coverage but higher premiums than ElderShield, addressing an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In particular, CareShield Life now offers lifetime cash payouts, especially for those with severe disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Indeed, it has better coverage, albeit with higher premiums, than the existing ElderShield scheme and is part of the Government’s initiatives to address the issue of our ageing population.

sections.label: Self-employed workers and home value threshold
sections.summary: MP asks how self-employed workers' concerns can be allayed and why the $13,000 home value threshold was used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how self-employed workers’ concerns can be allayed and help explain why the threshold of the home value of $ 13,000 was used?

sections.label: Derivation of withdrawal amount
sections.summary: MP asks how the withdrawal amount of $50 to $200 is derived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How is the withdrawal amount of $50-$200 derived?

sections.label: ElderShield400 opt-out and incentives
sections.summary: MP asks if ElderShield400 members will be reminded of the two-year penalty-free opt-out, noting incentives for those born before 1980.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Again, in the case of those on ElderShield400, come 2021, will they be reminded and advised that they have two years to opt out without any penalty?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would also like to point out that for those born before 1980, MOH has introduced incentives to join CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This applies whether they are already on ElderShield or had opted out previously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This group has a choice whether they wish to select CareShield Life or otherwise, and they can receive financial incentives, spread over a 10-year period, if they join within the next two years.

sections.label: Public education for informed choice
sections.summary: MP says sharing information will help this group understand their needs and decide, so a good public education exercise is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It will be good to share information with this group, so that they can better understand their needs, and give them the option to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, a good public education exercise will be needed.

sections.label: CareShield Life premiums at 30
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to explain clearly why Singaporeans must start paying CareShield Life premiums at age 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, I hope the Government can explain clearly why Singaporeans need to start to pay CareShield Life premiums at age 30.

sections.label: ElderShield premiums, payout, opt-outs
sections.summary: Under ElderShield, premiums start at age 40, the payout rate is 4%, and 36% of Singaporeans opted out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, under the current ElderShield, people only start to pay premiums when they reach 40 years old, and the payout rate is only 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, there are 36% of Singaporeans who opted out of ElderShield.

sections.label: ElderFund for first five years
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider using the recently established ElderFund to help pay premiums for the first five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government can consider using the recently established ElderFund to help pay for their premiums for the first five years.

sections.label: Automatic CareShield Life enrolment from 2020
sections.summary: From 2020, Singaporeans born in 1980 or after are automatically enrolled in CareShield Life regardless of pre-existing conditions or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: From 2020, all Singaporeans born in 1980 or after will automatically be enrolled into CareShield Life, regardless of pre-existing conditions or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Locally collected data showed that one in two healthy Singapore residents aged 65 today could become severely disabled in their lifetime.

sections.label: Claims versus premium collection concerns
sections.summary: The speaker says risk-pooling importance is diminished when people see $100 million in claims against $2.6 billion in premiums as at end-2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the sense of importance for risk-pooling is diminished when they observe that the total claim of $100 million is only a small fraction of the total premium collection of $2.6 billion as at end-2015. "What happens to the huge sum of money remaining in the pool?", they ask. “Who pockets the rest?”, the more cynical amongst them may also ask.

sections.label: CareShield Life universal long-term care coverage
sections.summary: CareShield Life ensures universal coverage and offers basic long-term care assurance for current and future generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: CareShield Life ensures universal coverage and offers basic long-term care assurance for the current and future generations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Severe disability statistics Singaporeans
sections.summary: Statistics show one in two Singaporeans will develop severe disabilities after age 65.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Statistics have shown that in Singapore, one out of two Singaporeans will develop severe disabilities after 65 years old.

sections.label: Women policyholders higher premiums
sections.summary: Women policyholders are expected to pay higher premiums than men, which stands out starkly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: (In English): Women policyholders are expected to pay a higher premium than men and this stands out starkly.

sections.label: Severe disability prevalence and CareShield Life
sections.summary: Statistics show severe disability prevalence among the aged in Singapore, US, UK and Japan, and CareShield Life provides better long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The statistics in Singapore and other developed countries, such as the US, UK and Japan, highlight just how prevalent severe disabilities are amongst their aged – in Singapore, one in two; in the US, also one in two; in the UK, eight in 10; and in Japan, the statistics are expected to triple in the next two decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Very importantly, CareShield Life provides better long-term care and protection for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This does not mean that the Government can cut back its support, this does not exonerate individuals from exercising personal responsibility, but this does enable us to pool our risks and help our fellow countrymen through times of need.

sections.label: Grown aged care capacity
sections.summary: Aged care capacity has grown, with targets of 10,000 home care and 6,200 day centre places by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: First, we have grown our aged care capacity significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We are on track to achieve 10,000 home care places and 6,200 day centre places by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For seniors who may need institutional care, we have added 1,200 community hospital beds and 5,300 nursing home beds since 2011.

sections.label: Eldercare centre access by 2020
sections.summary: By 2020, the aim is 90% of seniors having an eldercare centre within one kilometre of home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In fact, by 2020, we hope to provide 90% of seniors with access to an eldercare centre within a one-kilometre radius from their homes.

sections.label: CareShield Life future cohorts coverage
sections.summary: CareShield Life will provide universal coverage for future cohorts of Singaporeans born in 1980 or later.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For future cohorts, CareShield Life is not just an insurance scheme, but will be an important part of our social safety net.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: It will provide universal coverage for all future cohorts of Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, regardless of financial, health or disability status.

sections.label: CareShield Life fund injection
sections.summary: The Government will inject $100 million into the CareShield Life insurance fund to cover a significant portion of costs for future cohorts with pre-existing disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government will inject $100 million into the CareShield Life insurance fund to cover a significant portion of the costs of including Singaporeans in the future cohorts with pre-existing disabilities.

sections.label: ElderShield opt-out rates
sections.summary: ElderShield opt-out was 38% at 2002 launch, dropped to 5% in 2017, and about one in four in existing cohorts opted out.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: When ElderShield was launched in 2002, 38% of Singaporeans who were auto-enrolled opted out.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: While the opt-out rate has dropped to 5% in 2017, about one in four people in the existing cohorts have opted out of ElderShield.

sections.label: Incentives for existing cohorts
sections.summary: The Government will provide participation incentives to encourage existing cohorts to join CareShield Life within the first two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government will provide participation incentives to encourage existing cohorts to join CareShield Life within the first two years.

sections.label: Severely disabled and premiums
sections.summary: About 7% of Singaporeans aged 65 and above are severely disabled; including existing severely disabled cohorts would raise premiums about 30%, so the Government will support them through MediSave and ElderFund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The proportion of Singaporeans who are severely disabled at the older ages is much higher – about 7% of Singaporeans aged 65 and above today are severely disabled, compared to less than 0.1% of Singaporeans aged between 30 and 40.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Including the severely disabled from existing cohorts in CareShield Life would significantly increase premiums by about 30% for the rest of policyholders in these cohorts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government will support Singaporeans from existing cohorts who are already severely disabled and unable to join CareShield Life through other measures, including MediSave and ElderFund.

sections.label: Gender-differentiated CareShield Life premiums
sections.summary: The Committee decided gender-differentiated premiums for CareShield Life would more accurately reflect risk differences and result in a more actuarially fair and sustainable scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Committee did consider that women have less savings on average and could, therefore, be better supported by the men.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: However, on balance, the Committee decided that applying gender-differentiated premiums for CareShield Life would more accurately reflect the differences in risk between men and women and result in a more actuarially fair and sustainable scheme.

sections.label: CareShield Life premium payment age
sections.summary: CareShield Life premiums are paid only until age 67, although policyholders are covered for the rest of their lives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: On the other hand, CareShield Life premiums are only paid until the age of 67, although policyholders are covered for the rest of their lives.

sections.label: ElderShield claims by 2017
sections.summary: As at end of 2017, 15,600 policyholders had made ElderShield claims and benefited from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As at end of 2017, 15,600 policyholders have made ElderShield claims and benefited from the scheme.

sections.label: ElderShield assessors and assessments
sections.summary: Policyholders must see an appointed ElderShield assessor for disability assessment; there are 127 assessors, 13 providing home assessments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Today, in order to be assessed for ElderShield claims, policyholders will need to see an appointed ElderShield assessor, who will complete the ElderShield disability assessment for them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: There are currently 127 assessors, 13 of whom can provide home assessments.

sections.label: First assessment fee waived
sections.summary: The Government will waive the first assessment fee for all policyholders regardless of claim success, so the fee does not deter eligible policyholders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government will waive the first assessment fee for all policyholders, regardless of whether the claim is successful, so that the fee does not deter eligible policyholders, especially the lower-income, from making a claim.

sections.label: Improving disability assessment framework
sections.summary: The Government accepts recommendations to improve the disability assessment framework with clear guidance on cognitive impairment, so cognitively impaired policyholders more consistently qualify for claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the Committee heard feedback that it is not clear how ElderShield assessors should take into account the impact of an individual’s cognitive impairment on his ability to physically perform the ADLs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This can lead to inconsistent claim outcomes for ElderShield policyholders with cognitive impairments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We, therefore, accept the Committee’s recommendations to improve the disability assessment framework to provide clear guidance for disability assessors to consider policyholders’ ability to initiate a task, plan and, finally, complete an ADL effectively and safely.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: With the improvement to the assessment framework, assessors may also evaluate their ability to do so without being prompted to.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This ensures cognitively impaired policyholders with higher care needs will more consistently qualify for claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: CareShield Life, MediSave withdrawals for long-term care and ElderFund complement our efforts to build an inclusive and caring home for all of us as we age.

sections.label: Higher starting payouts
sections.summary: This improves on the current five- or six-year ElderShield payout duration, and the Government agrees to raise starting payouts from $400 to $600 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is an improvement over the current five- or six-year payout duration for ElderShield.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We also agree with the Committee’s recommendation to raise starting payouts from $400 to $600 per month, an increase of 50%.

sections.label: CareShield Life payout projection
sections.summary: Assuming 2% annual payout increases, a 30-year-old joining CareShield Life in 2020 would receive $1,200 per month if severely disabled at 67 or older.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If we assume that payouts increase by 2% per year, a 30-year-old who joins CareShield Life in 2020 will receive a payout amount of $1,200 per month if he becomes severely disabled at age 67 or older, if we assume 2% increase per annum.

sections.label: Premium impact of payout and criteria changes
sections.summary: Raising payouts from $600 to $800 and lowering criteria from three to two ADLs could raise the annual starting premium by more than two-thirds above $206.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To illustrate, if we raise the payout amount from $600 to $800 per month, premiums for a 30-year-old male in 2020 could increase by about one-third.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If we further lower the claims criteria from three to two ADLs, premiums will further increase by another one-third.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: So, as a result, if we combine both changes, the annual starting premium could be more than two-thirds higher than the currently proposed premium of $206 per year.

sections.label: Nursing home subsidies reduce fees
sections.summary: A $2,400 monthly nursing home fee can fall to $200 out-of-pocket after subsidies and other measures, under 10% of the original fee.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If the fee for nursing home care is about $2,400 per month, a lower middle-income Singaporean can receive Government subsidies of about $1,400, which reduces his fee to around $1,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Through the package of different measures, a nursing home bill of originally $2,400 reduces to $200 of out-of-pocket expenses, or less than 10% of the original nursing home fee.

sections.label: Means-tested subsidies for lower-income policyholders
sections.summary: The Government will provide means-tested subsidies of up to 30% for lower- and middle-income policyholders in properties with an AV of $21,000 or less.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: As Minster Gan explained in his opening speech, the Government will provide means-tested subsidies of up to 30% for lower- and middle-income policyholders living in a property with an AV of $21,000 or less.

sections.label: Transitional subsidies for future cohorts
sections.summary: Transitional subsidies will be provided to all Singapore Citizens in future cohorts for the first five years from the 2020 scheme launch.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In addition, we will provide transitional subsides to all Singapore Citizens in the future cohorts for the first five years from scheme launch in 2020.

sections.label: Family's monthly premium costs
sections.summary: A couple with two children would pay about $94 monthly for CareShield Life and MediShield Life, less than a quarter of their nearly $400 MediSave contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They have two children aged seven and 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
