sentences.text: So, in 2020, the couple’s CareShield Life premiums would be about $27 per month in total after means-tested subsidies and transitional subsidies, and their aggregate household MediShield Life premiums, including their children, add up to around $67 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For this family, the total premiums per month for both CareShield Life and MediShield Life is $94, which is less than a quarter of the couple’s combined MediSave contribution of almost $400 per month.

sections.label: Participation incentives reduce premiums
sections.summary: The Government will offer participation incentives of up to $2,500 to reduce premiums and encourage participation in the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government will offer participation incentives of up to $2,500 to reduce their premium and encourage participation in the scheme.

sections.label: ElderShield premiums and claims
sections.summary: Four Members asked why $3.3 billion in ElderShield premiums were collected while only $133 million was paid out as claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Ms Chia Yong Yong, Mr Zainal Sapari, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked why $3.3 billion in premiums for ElderShield were collected, and only $133 million were paid out as claims.

sections.label: Severe disability statistics question
sections.summary: Mr Pritam Singh asked about statistics of one in two Singaporeans aged 65 and above becoming severely disabled in their lifetimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the statistics of one in two Singaporeans aged 65 and above who become severely disabled in their lifetimes.

sections.label: Government administering CareShield Life
sections.summary: Mr Zainal Sapari asked about considerations for Government administration of CareShield Life instead of private insurers, with no change for existing ElderShield policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked about the considerations in having the Government administer CareShield Life instead of the private insurers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It also facilitates the provision of Government subsidies and financial support to Singaporeans and provides greater flexibility for the Government to make future enhancements to the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: There will be no change in contractual terms for ElderShield policyholders who choose to remain on their existing ElderShield 300 or 400 schemes.

sections.label: Monthly payouts starting 2020
sections.summary: Under this scheme, monthly payouts will start at $600 in 2020 and increase over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Under this scheme, monthly payouts will start at $600 in 2020 and increase over time.

sections.label: Subsidies and participation incentives
sections.summary: The Government will provide means-tested subsidies of up to 30%, transitional subsidies of up to $250, and participation incentives of up to $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government will provide means-tested subsidies of up to 30% for lower- and middle-income policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For Singapore Citizens born in 1980 or later, the Government will also provide transitional subsidies of up to $250 for the first five years from the launch of the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government will provide Singapore Citizens with participation incentives of up to $2,500 if they join within the first two years.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawals for disabled
sections.summary: From 2020, severely disabled Singaporeans aged 30 and above can withdraw up to $2,400 yearly from their own or spouses' MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: From 2020, severely disabled Singaporeans who are aged 30 and above can withdraw up to $2,400 every year from their own or their spouses' MediSave.

sections.label: Universal coverage for future cohorts
sections.summary: Universal coverage is introduced for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, covering pre-existing severe disabilities and low-income groups with premium support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It will be more than just an insurance scheme, but a key pillar of our social safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is why we are introducing universal coverage for future cohorts – Singaporeans born in 1980 or later – so that the scheme will cover all future generations, including those with pre-existing severe disabilities, as well as those who are low-income who need it the most as they will receive premium support.

sections.label: Premium subsidies and additional support
sections.summary: Means-tested premium subsidies are a permanent feature, and Additional Premium Support is extended to those unable to afford premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies for the low- to middle-income Singaporeans as a permanent feature of the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And for those who still are unable to afford their premiums after these subsidies and family support, we will extend Additional Premium Support to them.

sections.label: Cohort prefunding for sustainability
sections.summary: Each cohort will fund its own future needs through prefunding to ensure long-term sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To ensure long-term sustainability, each cohort will fund its own future needs through prefunding.

sections.label: MediSave, ElderFund, CareShield Life package
sections.summary: MediSave cash withdrawals for long-term care and ElderFund form a package with CareShield Life to strengthen long-term care financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: MediSave will be allowed to be withdrawn in cash to support long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Because the payout is in cash, it provides flexibility, whether one is cared for informally at home or formally through a provider or residential facility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We will set up ElderFund, an additional Government-funded safety net for low-income Singaporeans who are severely disabled and are in need of support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Together, the three initiatives – CareShield Life, use of MediSave for long-term care, and ElderFund – form a comprehensive package of measures that will significantly strengthen our long-term care financing.

sections.label: Urging support for Motion
sections.summary: Members of the House are urged to support the Motion and give Singaporeans better protection through CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: On that note, let me urge Members of this House to support the Motion, and give our fellow Singaporeans better protection and better assurance through CareShield Life.

sections.label: Two-billion budget for premium support
sections.summary: A $2-billion budget set aside by the Minister of Finance focuses on premium support subsidies, transitional subsidies and participation incentives, excluding running costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The $2-billion budget was set aside by the Minister of Finance in this year's Budget, and more details will be disclosed later on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But this fund focuses primarily on premium support subsidies, including transitional subsidies, as well as participation incentives, and the budget is still being finalised on exactly how much.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, the budget has to be worked out, and it would also depend on exactly how many people come on board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But it does not include the running costs of the scheme.

sections.label: CareShield Life cohort sizes
sections.summary: At the 2020 scheme start, the existing cohort may reach two million policyholders while the first 11 mandatory batches are estimated at about 600,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, at the start of the scheme in 2020, for instance, in the first few years, the existing cohort is definitely much larger than the mandatory cohort.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: There is a potential for up to two million policyholders to be in the CareShield Life scheme for the existing cohort whereas, for the mandatory cohort, for the first 11 batches, the estimate is about 600,000.

sections.label: Gender-differentiated premiums rationale
sections.summary: The speaker says gender differentiation was chosen over equal premiums because of adverse selection concerns and scheme unsustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I said earlier in my speech, yes, we could have designed it based on equal premiums but, as I have noted, I think we feel that, on balance, it is more prudent to do gender differentiation because of the concern about adverse selection and the unsustainability of the scheme.

sections.label: Explaining factors to industry
sections.summary: Chee Hong Tat said many factors are involved and the explanation will be shared with industry and professionals, including assumptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat has explained that quite a number of factors are involved and we will look at how best to explain this and share this with the industry and professionals in a meaningful way so that it is easier for people to understand, including the assumptions that the Member talked about.

sections.label: Exploring integration of schemes
sections.summary: The speaker says integrating some schemes or a different combination was explored but is complicated because risk factors and considerations differ.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To share with Members a secret, we did explore the possibilities of integrating some of them, or a different combination of them, but we find that it is going to be complicated because the risk factors are different and the considerations are different.

sections.label: Meaning of severe disability
sections.summary: A Member raises unanswered points and says clarity is wanted on what severe disability means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: I just wanted to also raise a number of other points perhaps that the Minister has not quite answered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: I think what we want to be very clear about is what is meant by severe disability.

sections.label: Phased rollout for system readiness
sections.summary: Phasing is used so IT and support systems are ready, starting in 2020 with 11 cohorts aged 30 to 40, close to 600,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The reason why we do it in phrases is because for a scheme involving so many people, we need to make sure that the information technology (IT) systems and the support systems are ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, if you look at the mandatory cohort, which the scheme will apply to first in 2020, we are looking at 11 cohorts, those aged 30 to 40 in 2020 – close to 600,000 people.

sections.label: MediSave use for long-term care
sections.summary: MediSave withdrawal for long-term care cash is available to anyone above 30 with severe disability, needing three ADLs, regardless of CareShield Life participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The second question is: can that person use his/her family members' MediSave as well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, you do not have to be participating in CareShield Life in order to tap on the MediSave withdrawal for cash for long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If you are on ElderShield or if you are not covered, it is available to anyone above the age of 30 who is suffering from severe disability, that means, you still need to be eligible as three ADLs.

sections.label: Spouse MediSave only
sections.summary: Only the MediSave account of a spouse may be tapped, not those of other family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Just to clarify that I mentioned in my speech that you are allowed to tap on the MediSave account of your spouse but not your other family members.

sections.label: Sharing CareShield Life assumptions
sections.summary: Many factors exist and the Council and actuaries will be consulted on how best to share CareShield Life information and assumptions meaningfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: His first question about the disclosure of information by the Council on the model and their assumptions, I think I have explained that in my speech that there are many factors and we will discuss with the Council and the actuaries on how best to share the information, the details and assumptions of CareShield Life in a meaningful way.

sections.label: CareShield Life fund returns
sections.summary: For CareShield Life the Government administers it, so all returns and additional balances stay in the fund for policyholders, with no profit or disbursement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this formula of saying, we share – 50% goes to the insurer, 50% goes back to the policyholders through a rebate – you need to specify it upfront because, otherwise, the insurer would not subsequently agree to give it back to policyholders if you do not spell it out clearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But for CareShield Life, it is different because the Government is going to administer it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: All the returns, all the additional balance amounts will stay within the fund for the benefit of policyholders, that it is not for profit, there will be no disbursement out of the fund.

sections.label: Higher payouts or lower premiums
sections.summary: Another way is to give higher payouts or reduce premium increases tied to higher payouts, and CPF investment approach will be discussed with CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But another way will be to give them a higher payout or reduce the premium increases associated with the higher payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And the last question that Mr Leon Perera raised about CPF investments, we will discuss with CPF Board on what is the approach that they will use.
